Kai: Quick sync — Polaris wants per-route SLAs and ability to buy "priority lanes" per endpoint.
Rosa: Clarify: priority lane = reserved QPS + lower queuing latency? or just routing priority?
Kai: Both. They asked for reserved capacity and a hard cap on public endpoints.
Ben: Billing: invoices are account-level today. We'll need endpoint_id in exports and a line item mapping.
Aisha: Ops: can only promise reserved latency on Dedicated pools. If they want hosted, we must limit guarantees.
Marco: Product proposal: ship MVP with API flag + billing export + contract template. Self-serve UI later.
Rosa: Launch criteria idea: (1) 3 pilot customers, (2) per-endpoint lines on invoices, (3) SRE runbook + rollback, (4) legal-approved clause.
LegalBot: Legal wants enumerated endpoints in order form and clear credit formula. Recommend credit cap at monthly endpoint spend.
Ben: Tech checklist:
- tag usage with endpoint_id
- accept priority_tier param on request
- billing mapper: endpoint_id -> invoice line
Marco: Timeline: 6 weeks for MVP (no self-serve). +3w for purchase flow.
Aisha: Risk: accounting complexity and ops churn if many endpoints sold. Recommend pilot limit 5 endpoints/customer.
Kai: Negotiation stance: offer flat reserved tiers for pilot (simple pricing), revisit usage-based later.
Rosa: Action items: Kai -> confirm pilot scope; Ben -> spike billing export (2d); Marco -> draft epic; LegalBot -> start clause.
product-bot: Created epic https://redwood.internal/epics/endpoint-lanes-5102024200
Kai: I'll update Polaris and push for pilot constraints.
Rosa: Closing thread for now — reopen if Polaris pushes for GA timing.
